judged_text: The single-object-to-array wrap is hand-maintained at ten-plus call sites with already-divergent empty values - handleNewBooking uses null while this and the other rebuilders use [] - and every rebuild-from-Booking path can only ever produce the organizer's calendar because Booking.destinationCalendar remains a single relation. The next event-builder contributor copies the null variant and silently drops destination calendars (the exact defect handleNewBooking ships in this diff), and any future consumer of rebuilt events that expects multi-host semantics gets only the first host's entry; one bookingDestinationCalendars helper would delete the duplicated ternaries and the divergence class.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces an inconsistency where most rebuilt CalendarEvent constructors use `destinationCalendar: ... ? [dc] : []`, but `handleNewBooking` sets it to `null` when neither `eventType.destinationCalendar` nor `organizerUser.destinationCalendar` exists (apps/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts: `: null`). Immediately after, collective-team logic does `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars);` so when it is `null` the push is skipped and collected team member destination calendars are silently dropped. This is a concrete behavior defect visible in the diff. The duplicated ternaries / divergent empty values across many call sites are also evident, but the null-vs-array issue in `handleNewBooking` specifically causes lost destination calendars.
